evidence.claim: Utah DOT describes this state scenic byway as a 40-mile drive through Cedar Canyon and Dixie National Forest, allowing an hour between Cedar City and Long Valley Junction.
evidence.quote: This state scenic byway takes you through Cedar Canyon and the Dixie National Forest, following SR-14 for 40 miles between Cedar City and Long Valley Junction at US-89. Allow an hour for this drive.

evidence.claim: The Cedar City–Long Valley Junction road entered the state highway system in 1912 and received the number SR 14 in the 1920s.
evidence.quote: The road from SR-1 (by 1926 US-91, now SR-130) in Cedar City to SR-11 (US-89) at Long Valley Junction was added to the state highway system in 1912 and numbered SR-14 in the 1920s.

evidence.claim: A branch to Cedar Breaks joined it in 1927; that branch later became part of SR 148.
evidence.quote: A branch from Cedar Breaks Junction to Cedar Breaks National Monument was added in 1927, but in 1931 it was renumbered SR-55, and is now part of SR-148.
